minutes.headline: Committee ratified a new three-year teachers' contract and endorsed a Brooks House sale/lease study for town meeting.
minutes.summary: The School Committee approved a line-item transfer, PTO donations, the facilities/grounds report, a menu of ARPA-eligible capital projects, and several warrant-article recommendations ahead of the November 12 special town meeting, including Chapter 70 funding and a study on selling or leasing the Brooks House. It also ratified, by roll call, a new multi-year contract with the teachers' union (LEA) covering raises, leave and retirement provisions, and adopted its own and the superintendent's annual goals.

budget_items.topic: High school office-supply to "fizzed" line transfer
budget_items.what_was_said: Money is being moved from the high school office-supply line to the fizzed line so a purchase can be made; described as a small amount after initial confusion.
A member questioned paying the annual NEAS accreditation fee, calling the increase notice arbitrary; another asked what would happen if the district didn't pay.
PTO donated Penny Wars fundraiser proceeds to the gift account, earmarked for a shade structure at Turkey Hill.
PTO donated Scholastic Book Fair proceeds to the gift account, earmarked for the library.
Total warrants for the period were reported to the committee.
Vendor determined existing PA cabling could not be reused for 911 phone lines, requiring cabling the whole building at a cost well above what was budgeted for the project.

An updated site-walk quote for the generator came in far higher than an earlier phone quote; it would only power heat and kitchen, not the whole building, though a later correction said it does power the whole building.

budget_items.topic: Mini-split project phase 2 / building management system tie-in
budget_items.what_was_said: Cost to connect remaining mini-splits to the building management system; a green communities grant, if awarded, would cover about half.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill door replacement and vestibule
budget_items.what_was_said: Engineers believe allocated money covers the door replacement but not the vestibule buildout, which would cost significantly more.
Fire alarm must be upgraded to full code rather than component replacement, adding cost beyond what was allocated.
Filling the funding gap for the cabling project was named as a top priority for any available ARPA money, though it may not be eligible since the work is already complete.
New teachers' contract sets COLA increases across three years, applying to both the salary schedule and the athletic/extracurricular schedule.

budget_items.topic: LEA contract longevity and retirement payments
budget_items.what_was_said: Teachers with 30 years of service get a longevity payment added to base salary; those retiring after 20 years with 100 accumulated sick days can get a one-time payment based on a per-day rate up to a cap.
Finance committee voted 5-0 to recommend the amount in Article 2.
Finance committee reported the new design group's estimate for the municipal building project came in high enough that phase one is not funded and the borrowing article will not move forward.

budget_items.topic: PTO fundraisers and requests for funding
budget_items.what_was_said: PTO reported fundraiser proceeds and gear sales, a large take from a prior dance, and that it is offering per-school funding to teachers who apply for classroom requests.
The RFP for design services came in under budget by this amount, reported as good news.

what_happened.line: Committee ratified a new three-year contract with the teachers' union by unanimous roll call, setting cost-of-living raises for three years.
Committee voted unanimously to recommend a study on selling or long-term leasing the Brooks House at the November 12 special town meeting.
Committee also voted to recommend the Chapter 70 funding article at the same special town meeting.
Several facility projects -- 911 compliance cabling, the primary school generator, and a fire alarm upgrade -- came in over their budgeted allocations.
Committee agreed no budget update for next year will be given until January.

why_it_matters: The new teachers' contract sets pay increases across three years that will show up in future school budgets and, in turn, the town's tax bill.
The Brooks House study, if the special town meeting approves it, could lead toward a future vote on selling or leasing a town-owned property.

The facility cost overruns on 911 cabling, the generator and the fire alarm mean the capital plan may need more money than was budgeted, a gap the committee discussed covering with leftover ARPA funds.
